title: Designing Interfaces: Patterns for Effective Interaction Design
extraction_notes: Title and authors verified on PDF page 3; edition, copyright, January 2020 publication and ISBN on PDF page 4. The copyright page also records first release 2019-12-18.

All page ranges are inclusive and 1-based. Printed Arabic page n maps to PDF page n+20 throughout the twelve chapters. Chapter PDF boundaries include trailing blank pages. Their printed_end is null because the blank page has no visible numeral; printed_last_content_page gives the preceding numbered page.

Used pypdf text extraction, actually displayed and read in bounded output passes. Extraction alone was not counted as reading. A truncated attempt at chapter 10 was reread in bounded complete passes; an uncertain chapter 1 page was reread in full.

Text extraction includes occasional line-break hyphenation, split words, and text/caption reading-order artifacts. Images cannot be understood from extraction alone. Selected pages were separately rendered with pypdfium2 and inspected with view_image; only those are in figure_checks.

Full-study denotes completed study of decision-relevant chapter prose with any explicit historical example-gallery exclusions shown below. It does not mean every source image was visually inspected or every page of the entire book was read.

Exclusions in chapters 2, 3, and 8 are repetitive historical product example galleries after the corresponding pattern explanations. These galleries may contain contextual example prose, which is deliberately not claimed as fully read. All other chapter text, including its example prose and captions, was read.

Front matter was consulted for metadata and contents, not read comprehensively. Index and back matter (PDF 581–602) were excluded as navigation/production material rather than design instruction. Book files, extracted text and rendered figures are not included in the repository.

Current platform/security/accessibility specifications require current primary sources. Historical app screenshots, market shares, exact pixel/font/timing values, inter-app constraints, password rules and framework recommendations are not carried forward as authoritative requirements.

chapters.title: Designing for People
chapters.notes: Read all extracted chapter text, including research framing and all cognition/behavior patterns. Retained goals, evidence, safe exploration, deferred decisions, interruption, stable spatial cues, and fluent repetition. Social-engagement examples are not goals to impose on users. No chapter figure checks were required for these prose-based principles.

chapters.title: Layout of Screen Elements
chapters.notes: Read all extracted text, pattern details, and example captions. Visually inspected hierarchy, density, and proximity figures. Retained semantic hierarchy, useful grouping, visual framework, task emphasis, comparison-aware disclosure, and persistent workspace considerations. Remaining figures were not comprehensively inspected. Numerical emphasis ratios and sample layout choices are contextual rather than universal.

chapters.title: Visual Style and Aesthetics
chapters.notes: Read all extracted text and captions, including color, typography, image/icon style, emotional expression, density, metaphors, skeuomorphism, flat/minimal styles, and adaptation. Visually inspected the four design variants and spacious/crowded comparison. Other examples were not comprehensively visually inspected. Retained intent, readability, coherent visual semantics, cultural context, and task-appropriate expression. Historical font-size defaults, broad emotional color claims, and universal style preferences were not promoted to requirements; illustrations do not prove outcomes.

chapters.title: Mobile Interfaces
chapters.notes: Read all extracted text and all pattern/example captions. Applied mobile context, reentry, reduced input effort, first useful content, target hit area, loading feedback, and device capability reasoning. No chapter screenshots were separately visually inspected; retained principles are supported by prose, not inferred screenshot details. Explicitly rejected historical market/device constraints, exact pixel budgets, and old inter-app restrictions. Bottom Navigation denotes a mobile-web footer, not native iOS tab navigation. Current iOS guidance must supply platform specifications.

chapters.title: Lists of Things
chapters.notes: Read all extracted text, all pattern mechanics, and example captions. Compared overview, finding, browsing, manipulation, split view, drilldown, inlay, cards, thumbnails, carousels, pagination, jump/index navigation, and item creation. Retained content/cardinality/task fit, return context, realistic long/short content, and comparison costs. No individual chapter screenshot was visually inspected; product examples are historical illustrations, not measured validation.

chapters.notes: Read the action/control introduction, each pattern explanation, and conclusion. Listed intervening historical screenshot/example galleries were excluded from systematic full study; incidental previews of some examples do not change this conservative ledger. Retained affordance, input alternatives, scope, grouping, commitment, preview, loading, cancellation, undo/history, and repetition. No gallery image supports a retained visual claim. Backend operation boundaries must qualify cancellation/undo promises; timing and undo-depth examples are not universal thresholds.

chapters.title: Showing Complex Data
chapters.notes: Read all extracted text, pattern explanations, and captions. Visually inspected stacked-bar rearrangement, common-x separate-y charts, and small multiples. Retained question-led encoding, meaningful comparison, overview/detail, exact values, filtering/highlighting, linked selection, and space constraints. Other figures not comprehensively visually inspected. Multi-Y Graph is specifically separate vertical plots sharing x; it does not license misleading overlaid dual axes. No universal perceptual-speed guarantee is asserted. The final PDF page is blank and has no visible printed label; printed_end is null, and printed_last_content_page records the preceding numbered content page.

chapters.title: Getting Input from Users: Forms and Controls
chapters.notes: Read all extracted text and captions, including every form principle and pattern: forgiving/structured formats, sentence inputs, hints/prompts, password feedback, autocomplete, complex choosers, list builders, defaults, errors, and conclusion. Visually inspected the three-state Mailchimp registration example. Retained minimized effort, persistent labels, localization, rejectable assistance, visible correction, and success. Blanket disabled-submit advice and historical password composition examples are explicitly not adopted as current universal or security requirements. Other screenshots were not comprehensively inspected. The final PDF page is blank and has no visible printed label; printed_end is null, and printed_last_content_page records the preceding numbered content page.

chapters.title: User Interface Systems and Atomic Design
chapters.notes: Read all extracted text and captions, including the entire historical UI-framework tour. Visually inspected the Fluent iOS/Android picker examples. Retained modularity, shared style/behavior, real-content assembly, platform variants, and a design system that enables rather than constrains good design. The framework catalog, popularity claims, and assertions about automatically solved browser/responsive issues were assessed but excluded from current implementation recommendations. Web frameworks are not native iOS specifications.

chapters.title: Beyond and Behind the Screen
chapters.notes: Read the complete short chapter. Assessed connected devices, anticipatory/assistive systems, natural interfaces, scenario thinking, and ethical human-centered intent. Retained only contextual awareness and limits in the synthesis; excluded new implementation prescriptions because this overview does not provide enough method or evidence for current AI/IoT design. No illustrations appear in this chapter. The final PDF page is blank and has no visible printed label; printed_end is null, and printed_last_content_page records the preceding numbered content page.

figure_checks.inspection: Rendered PDF page viewed. The upward stack runs from data/content through functionality/input/output to presentation; the start cue points to data/content. Supports structuring information before screen appearance, not a compulsory waterfall process.

Rendered PDF page viewed. One central node links bidirectionally to five outer nodes, with no outer-node connections shown. Confirms why moving between destinations can require a return through a hub; does not establish the best topology for all mobile apps.

Rendered PDF page viewed. Example B uses aligned blocks, a prominent upper region and an orderly secondary area; A distributes competing unaligned blocks. Used for hierarchy reasoning, not a measured claim of faster task performance.

Rendered PDF page viewed. The denser left arrangement keeps related blocks and text together; the looser right separates each region more evenly. Supports evaluating relationships rather than maximizing whitespace.

Rendered PDF page viewed. Paired diagrams show the same layout with group boundaries annotated on the right: header, repeated upper group and two distinct lower groups. Supports grouping by proximity and meaningful alignment.

Rendered PDF page viewed. Four Friendly banking concepts vary imagery, palette, alignment, typography and promotional emphasis. They are not identical-content controlled experiments; retained only as evidence that coordinated visual choices create different presentations.

figure_checks.description: Figure 5-18: spacious and crowded visual design
figure_checks.inspection: Rendered PDF page viewed. The left composition separates headline, supporting text and button; the right compresses headline/body/action into a tight vertical group. Supports evaluating spacing and tone in context, not a universal spacious-is-better rule.
Rendered PDF page viewed. The light-blue series moves from the tops of stacked bars to a common baseline, exposing small height differences. Supports comparison-aware encoding.

Rendered PDF page viewed. Oil price level and daily percentage change appear in vertically separated plots aligned to a common timeline. Confirms that this pattern is not an arbitrary overlaid dual-axis chart.

figure_checks.description: Figure 9-27: geographic and demographic small multiples
figure_checks.inspection: Rendered PDF page viewed. Repeated US maps form an income-by-demographic matrix with common geometry and color conventions. Small labels and many maps illustrate the space/legibility cost; the figure does not demonstrate fitness for a phone viewport.

Rendered PDF page viewed. Three form states show a disabled initial action, enabled action after password entry despite missing username, then a summary alert plus a local username error. Retained for feedback placement and whole-sequence review, not as a recommendation for this validation strategy or password policy.

figure_checks.description: Figures 11-3 and 11-4: Fluent iOS and Android date/time pickers
figure_checks.inspection: Rendered PDF page viewed. The same design-system component category has different platform presentations. Used for semantic/system coherence with platform variation; historical screenshots are not current iOS/Android specifications.
